explanation: A young king of Judah who introduced religious reforms and removed idolatry from the kingdom.
High priest in the temple during King Josiah's reign, who found the Book of the Law (the Torah).
Scribe and official in King Josiah's court, who helped convey the discovery of the Book of the Law.
A scroll containing God's laws and commands, likely part of the books of Moses, which was found in the temple.
A change or improvement of something, in this case Josiah's attempt to restore monotheism and remove idolatry.
Worship of false gods or idols, which was forbidden according to the discovered Book of the Law.
A prophetess who confirmed the authenticity of the Book of the Law and predicted that God's judgment would come upon Judah.
